message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are earned by being the first to empty your hand in each round. | After each round, the winner tallies the values of all cards left in opponents’ hands. Those numbers become the winner’s score for that round. | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each + 8 Wild cards (4 “Wild”, 4 “Wild Draw Four”). | 2–10 of each color, 2 “Skip”, 2 “Reverse”, 2 “Draw Two” per color. | | **Setup** | 2–10 players. Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile. Turn the top card face‑up to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, follow the “starting‑card” rule (see below). | The player to the dealer’s left starts. | | **Turn Order** | Clockwise, unless a “Reverse” card changes direction. | Each turn consists of two parts: 1) play a card (or draw), 2) optionally play a second card if it matches the first. | | **Playing a Card** | You may play a card that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top discard. Wild cards match any color. | Example: top card is Red 5 → you can play any Red card, any 5, or a Wild. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and skips their turn. | Wild Draw Four may only be played if you have no other playable card. If challenged and you were wrong, you must draw 4 cards instead of the opponent drawing. | | **Drawing** | If you cannot play a card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | If the draw pile runs out, reshuffle the discard pile (except the top card) to form a new draw pile. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, you must shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. | If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two cards as a penalty. | | **Winning a Round** | The first player to discard all their cards wins the round. | The winner scores points equal to the sum of all cards still held by opponents. | | **Winning the Game** | First player to reach 500 points (or your chosen target) wins the game. | If you’re playing a single round, the winner of that round is the overall winner. | --- ### Quick Play‑by‑Play Example 1. **Dealer** deals 7 cards each. 2. Top card of discard pile: **Yellow 7**. 3. Player A (to dealer’s left) has **Yellow 9**, **Red 7**, **Blue Skip**. - Plays **Yellow 9** (matches color). 4. Player B has **Green 9**, **Yellow Reverse**. - Plays **Yellow Reverse** (matches color). - Direction changes to counter‑clockwise. 5. Player C (now next) has **Red 5**, **Blue 9**. - No match → draws a card. - Drawn card is **Red 5** → plays it. 6. Player D has **Wild**. - Plays **Wild**, chooses **Red**. 7. Player A now must play a Red card. - Plays **Red 7** → wins the round if it was their last card. --- ### Common House Rules | Rule | Description | |------|-------------| | **No “Draw Two” on “Draw Four”** | Some players allow a “Draw Two” to be played after a “Wild Draw Four” if the next player has no other playable card. | | **“Uno” Penalty** | Instead of drawing two cards, the penalty can be “draw four” or “draw six” depending on house preference. | | **Scoring** | Some groups score only the winner’s points, others also subtract the loser’s points. | | **Multiple Rounds** | Play until a player reaches a target score (e.g., 500). | --- ### Tips for New Players 1. **Keep track of colors** – It’s easier to play when you have a variety of colors in your hand. 2. **Save “Wild Draw Four”** – Use it when you’re stuck and the next player has many cards. 3. **Watch the discard pile** – Knowing what’s been played helps you anticipate opponents’ moves. 4. **Call “UNO” early** – Don’t wait until the last second; you’ll be less likely to forget. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
